title: Hotel revenue review deck with restated prior year and comp-set indices
prompt:
Build the 2025 revenue review for Calloway Hotels, a group of five city hotels, presented by VP Revenue Strategy Elena Marchetti to the ownership board on 12 February 2026. Every figure must come from your own analysis of hotel_monthly.csv (rooms available, rooms sold and room revenue per hotel and month for 2024 and 2025, with 2024 as originally reported), compset_2025.csv (the same three measures for each hotel's competitive set in 2025) and restatements_2024.json (three corrections to the 2024 figures).

Definitions: occupancy = rooms sold / rooms available; ADR = room revenue / rooms sold; RevPAR = room revenue / rooms available. Any group of hotels or months is aggregated by summing rooms and revenue first, never by averaging ratios. Every 2024 comparison uses the restated 2024 figures. MPI, ARI and RGI are the hotel's occupancy, ADR and RevPAR divided by its competitive set's, times 100. Split the RevPAR change into an occupancy effect = (2025 occupancy - 2024 occupancy) × 2024 ADR and a rate effect = (2025 ADR - 2024 ADR) × 2025 occupancy. Show occupancy and growth rates with one decimal, ADR and RevPAR in dollars and cents, indices with one decimal.

1. 'Calloway Hotels 2025 Revenue Review' (presenter, audience, date)

4. 'RevPAR by hotel': dumbbell chart of restated 2024 and 2025 RevPAR for each hotel, hotels sorted by 2025 RevPAR from highest at the top, YoY % beside each row

6. 'Fair share vs the competitive set': table of each hotel's 2025 MPI, ARI and RGI; cells at or above 100.0 tinted green, below 100.0 tinted red

8. 'Restating 2024': the three corrections, then 2024 portfolio occupancy, ADR and RevPAR as reported next to restated
9. 'Seasonality by hotel': five small multiples of monthly RevPAR, restated 2024 dashed and 2025 solid, all panels sharing one y-axis scale
10. 'Pricing actions for 2026': three actions

title: A/B test readout deck with confidence intervals, SRM check and a forest plot
prompt:
Build the readout deck for experiment EXP-2291, the one-page checkout test at Brightcart, a grocery delivery app. Product analytics lead Sofia Lindqvist presents it to the product leadership team on 8 October 2026 and asks for a ship decision. Analyze daily_results.csv (per day, variant, platform and user type: checkout sessions, orders and revenue) and experiment.json (design, allocation, alpha and guardrails).

Method: the unit is the checkout session. Conversion p = orders / sessions per arm. The difference d = p_treatment - p_control has a 95% CI of d ± 1.96 × sqrt(p_c(1 - p_c)/n_c + p_t(1 - p_t)/n_t); relative lift = d / p_control and its CI is the CI of d divided by p_control. The p-value is two-sided from the pooled z-test z = d / sqrt(p̄(1 - p̄)(1/n_c + 1/n_t)), p̄ being the pooled rate. The sample ratio check is a chi-square test of the two arms' sessions against the planned 50/50 split (1 degree of freedom). Each arm's own 95% CI is p ± 1.96 × sqrt(p(1 - p)/n). The cumulative lift on day k uses all data from day 1 to day k. AOV = revenue / orders; revenue per session = revenue / sessions. Rates in percent with two decimals, lifts with one, p-values with three.

Exactly 11 slides, titled:
1. 'One-Page Checkout: Experiment Readout' (experiment ID, presenter, date)
2. 'The decision': a one-sentence ship recommendation and tiles for control and treatment conversion, relative lift with its 95% CI, and the p-value
3. 'Experiment design': diagram of checkout sessions split 50/50 into control and treatment boxes (each describing its checkout), dates, primary metric and both guardrails
4. 'Sample ratio check': sessions per arm, expected per arm, the chi-square statistic, its p-value and a pass or fail badge
5. 'Conversion by arm': two bars with 95% CI error bars and value labels on a y-axis that starts at 0%
6. 'Lift over time': cumulative relative lift for the 28 days as a line with a shaded 95% CI band and a zero line, the first day from which the lower bound stays above zero annotated
7. 'Lift by segment': forest plot of relative lift with 95% CI for iOS, Android, Web, New and Returning sorted by lift, largest at the top, plus the overall result as a diamond at the bottom; a vertical zero line; segments whose CI includes zero drawn with hollow markers
8. 'Guardrails': AOV and revenue per session for both arms with the change and a pass or fail badge against each guardrail in experiment.json
9. 'Platform detail': table of iOS, Android and Web with sessions, conversion per arm, relative lift, 95% CI and p-value
10. 'Rollout plan': timeline 10% (13 Oct) → 50% (20 Oct) → 100% (27 Oct) with a kill-switch criterion
11. 'Appendix: statistical method'

Design system: define the palette as CSS custom properties on :root named --bg (#FFFFFF), --ink (#111827), --muted (#6B7280), --control (#94A3B8) and --treatment (#7C3AED), and use them for every themed color. Inter only. Slides 2-11: an h2 in Inter 700 at 32px whose left edge is 64px from the slide edge at the same top on every slide, a small pill at the top right reading 'EXP-2291', and a footer with 'Brightcart · Product Analytics' on the left and 'n / 11' on the right. Charts as inline SVG with titled axes; no text under 12px.

T toggles a dark theme by setting data-theme='dark' on the html element, which overrides only --bg to #0F172A, --ink to #F1F5F9 and --muted to #CBD5E1; the choice persists across reloads. Every slide has speaker notes in a hidden aside with class notes, and N toggles a notes panel. The slide 4 notes must give the SRM p-value; the slide 7 notes must name the segments whose CI includes zero.

title: Subscription cohort retention deck with triangle heatmap, layer cake and payback
prompt:
Build a retention deep dive for Lexio, a language-learning app with a monthly subscription, presented by head of growth Marcus Obi at the leadership offsite on 14 October 2026. Work from subscriptions.csv (one row per subscriber who started between October 2025 and September 2026: start month, acquisition channel, promo code, monthly price and last paid month) and acquisition.json (data cutoff, app store fee, acquisition spend by channel and the spring promo).

Definitions: month 0 is the start month; a subscriber is retained in month k if last_paid_month is at least k months after start_month. A cohort's month-k retention = retained in month k / cohort size. Pooled month-k retention sums retained subscribers and cohort sizes over every cohort observed through month k (never average percentages). Net revenue = price × (1 - app store fee) for each month paid. Cumulative net revenue per starting subscriber through month k = net revenue collected in months 0 to k / subscribers, over cohorts observed through month k; 6-month LTV is its value at month 5. CAC = channel spend / channel subscribers. Payback month = the first k where cumulative net revenue per starting subscriber reaches CAC. Paying subscribers at the cutoff have last_paid_month 2026-09; MRR is the sum of their monthly prices. Retention with one decimal (whole percents in the heatmap), dollars with two decimals.

title: Plant OEE review deck with loss waterfall, Pareto and X-bar/R control chart
prompt:
Prepare the February 2026 performance review of Norvik Packaging's Hartwell plant (four bottling lines, two shifts), presented by plant manager Jonas Berg to the operations leadership team on 10 March 2026. Analyze shifts_feb2026.csv (per day, line and shift: planned minutes, downtime minutes, total and good units), downtime_events.csv (every stop with its reason and minutes), fill_weight_l3.csv (25 hourly subgroups of five fill weights from Line 3 on 24 February) and lines.json (ideal rates, targets and control-chart constants).

Definitions, all time-based so any group of shifts or lines aggregates by summing minutes first: run time = planned - downtime; net run time = total units / ideal rate; fully productive time = good units / ideal rate. Availability = run / planned, performance = net run / run, quality = fully productive / net run, OEE = fully productive / planned (= A × P × Q). Losses: downtime = planned - run, speed loss = run - net run, quality loss = net run - fully productive. Control chart: X̿ = mean of the subgroup means, R̄ = mean of the subgroup ranges, X̄ limits X̿ ± A2·R̄, R chart upper limit D4·R̄. A point is out of control if its mean is outside the X̄ limits, if it is one of 7 or more consecutive means on the same side of X̿ (flag every point in such a run), or if its range is above the R limit. Percentages one decimal, hours one decimal, grams two decimals.

Exactly 11 slides, titled:
1. 'Hartwell Plant Review · February 2026' (presenter, audience, date)
2. 'Plant at a glance': tiles for plant OEE, availability, performance, quality and good units
3. 'OEE by line': bars sorted from highest OEE, availability, performance and quality printed under each bar, a dashed 85% world-class line and a solid 70% target line
4. 'Where the time went': waterfall in hours from planned time through downtime, speed loss and quality loss to fully productive time

6. 'Shift A vs shift B': OEE per line for each shift as grouped bars, the line with the largest gap annotated with the gap in points
7. 'Fill weight control · Line 3': X̄ chart above R chart sharing the subgroup axis 1-25, center lines and limits labeled with their values, out-of-control points in red
8. 'Line scorecard': table of line, planned hours, availability, performance, quality, OEE and top downtime reason with its minutes; OEE below 70% in red
9. 'Line 2 changeover plan': current vs target changeover as two horizontal stacked bars (current: clean 14, tooling swap 18, adjust 12, first-off check 8 minutes; target: 8, 10, 6, 6)
10. 'Actions and owners': three actions, each with an owner and a date
11. 'Appendix: definitions and control rules'
